turns.prompt_text: In Google Photos, can I see only photos in which are not in an album?
turns.response_html:
Currently, Google Photos does not have a native filter or search command to view only photos that are not in any album. This is a frequently requested feature, but as of now, the app does not support it directly.

However, there is a common workaround using the Archive feature to isolate these photos temporarily.

The "Archive" Workaround

This method involves hiding all photos that are in albums so that only the "un-albumed" photos remain visible in your main view.

  1. Open an Album: Go to the Library tab and open one of your albums.
  2. Select All Photos: Select every photo in that album (on a computer, you can use Shift + click to select large ranges).
  3. Archive Them: Click the three-dot menu and select Move to Archive.
    • Note: Archiving hides photos from your main "Photos" timeline but keeps them in their albums and search results. It does not delete them.
  4. Repeat: Do this for every album you have.
  5. View the Results: Return to your main Photos tab. Since you have archived everything that belongs to an album, the only photos remaining in this view are the ones that are not in any album.

Important: If you want to return your library to its original state, you will need to go to the Archive folder, select the photos, and choose Unarchive. However, this will mix them back into the main view with the photos that were never in an album.
